title: EPIC: Efficient Predicate-Guided Inference-Time Control for Compositional Text-to-Image Generation
claim: Existing scaling strategies give coarse or costly feedback; ours parses the task once into structured checks for efficient controlled refinement.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right, ours highlighted with a bold border
description: Three side-by-side rounded panels compare inference-time strategies for text-to-image generation. The left panel, Selection/Search Scaling, shows a prompt feeding an image model that produces a grid of candidate images, and a scalar verifier (magnifying glass) picks one. Its caption reads 'Coarse feedback with limited control'. The middle panel, Agentic Refinement, shows a loop of prompt and image, an MLLM critique (brain icon), a checklist, an MLLM plan and an image model. Its caption reads 'Flexible feedback with high MLLM cost'. The right panel, EPIC (Ours), has a bold black border. A prompt goes through an MLLM parse into a fixed predicate program, then an inner loop of image model, predicate verifier and refinement policy. Its caption reads 'Structured feedback with efficient control'. Red labels mark MLLM calls, and the eye is drawn to the bold right panel.
caption: Comparison of inference-time scaling strategies for compositional text-to-image generation. Selection/search scaling uses scalar feedback to choose among many candidates, while agentic refinement obtains flexible feedback through repeated MLLM critique and planning. EPIC instead parses the prompt once into a fixed predicate program and uses predicate-level verification to provide structured feedback for efficient refinement control.
abstract: Recent text-to-image (T2I) generators can synthesize realistic images, but still struggle with compositional prompts involving multiple objects, counts, attributes, and relations. We introduce EPIC (Efficient Predicate-Guided Inference-Time Control), a training-free inference-time refinement framework for compositional T2I generation. EPIC casts refinement as predicate-guided search: it parses the original prompt once into a visual program of object variables and typed predicates, then verifies each candidate image against this program using visual evidence extracted from that image. A candidate is judged to satisfy the prompt when all predicates pass; otherwise, unmet predicates guide the next step, routing localized failures to targeted editing and layout-level or persistent failures to resampling. On GenEval2, EPIC improves the prompt-level Soft-TIFA GM score from 34.16% for single-pass generation to 71.46%. With the same generator, editor, and image-model execution budget, EPIC outperforms the strongest baseline by 19.23 points. It also uses 31% fewer image-model executions, 72% fewer multimodal large language model (MLLM) calls, and 81% fewer MLLM tokens per prompt.
